title: Consumption prepaid collateral bundles & trial mechanisms (product brief)
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This brief defines the product concept, requirements, and rollout plan for a new pricing construct: prepaid collateral bundles (PCB) that customers purchase as locked credits to cover reserved capacity, burstable consumption, and trial allowances. The goal is to provide customers predictable economics for adoption, protect Redwood from uncollectible usage, and enable frictionless trials with configurable safety controls.

Goals

- Enable predictable short-to-medium term revenue by letting customers prepay for capacity or credit pools.
- Reduce fraud/chargeback exposure for large trial activations and high-burst customers.
- Make trials and onboarding smooth: automatic trial-to-paid conversion with configurable grace periods.
- Provide clear UX and reconciliation pathways so finance and customer success can explain charges.

Scope

In scope: design of PCB SKUs, API surface for creating/redeeming collateral bundles, billing reconciliation logic, UI flows for sales and self-serve, rules for expiration/refunds, SLOs and telemetry.
Out of scope: wholesale changes to invoicing cadence, international tax treatment (handled by existing billing stack), on-prem private deployment billing connectors (future phase).

Definitions

- Collateral bundle (CB): a purchasable item representing prepaid credits (token-credits + optional reserved capacity hours).
- Collateral ledger: immutable event log of deposits, redemptions, refunds, and expirations.
- Trial collateral: temporary CB granted to new customers for evaluation; tracked separately for conversion rules.
- Reserved capacity carveout: portion of a CB that guarantees dedicated capacity for a time window.

High-level product hypothesis

If customers can prepay collateral in discrete bundles with clear conversion rules and guardrails, we will increase early revenue recognition, reduce overage disputes, and increase conversion from trial to paid usage while limiting exposure to high-cost bursts.

Requirements (PRD style)

1) SKU model and UI
  - 3 initial SKUs: Starter-CB (100k tokens), Grow-CB (1M tokens + 10 reserved GPU-hours), Enterprise-CB (5M tokens + 100 reserved GPU-hours).
  - Each SKU has: price_usd, token_quantity, optional_reserved_capacity_hours, expiration_days, refundable_percent.
  - UI: Billing > Prepaid Credits page to purchase, view balance, and configure auto-topup thresholds.

2) API surface (stable public endpoints)
  - POST /v1/bundles.create => create collateral bundle (payment & ledger entry)
  - GET /v1/bundles/{id} => retrieve bundle metadata and remaining balance
  - POST /v1/bundles/{id}/redeem => redeem credits for request (internal use by runtime router)
  - POST /v1/bundles/{id}/convert => convert trial collateral to paid order (on acceptance)
  - POST /v1/bundles/{id}/refund => issue refund according to refundable_percent and policy

  Example create request (JSON):
  {
    "sku": "Grow-CB",
    "customer_id": "acct_01Gq2x...",
    "payment_method_id": "pm_0a1b2c",
    "metadata": { "sales_rep": "sr-122" }
  }

3) Runtime integration and prioritized routing
  - Router must accept an optional header X-Prepaid-Bundle: {bundle_id} to consume from a specific CB.
  - If a request cannot be fulfilled due to reserved capacity limits, runtime should fall back per routing policy (e.g., use hosted pool and mark as overage against CB if allowed).
  - Redemption semantics: atomic decrement of token count and reserved hour counters, with idempotency and optimistic locking.

4) Reconciliation and ledger
  - All bundle events generate ledger entries: DEPOSIT, REDEEM, EXPIRE, REFUND, CONVERT.
  - Daily reconciliation job aggregates ledger to billing invoices and posts to AR system. Jobs must be idempotent and have auditable run logs.

5) Trials and conversion rules
  - Trial CBs: expire in 30 days, refundable_percent = 0, conversion window = 72 hours after trial acceptance.
  - Auto-convert behavior (opt-in): if trial usage exceeds threshold (e.g., 75% of trial tokens), optionally create a paid Grow-CB and apply remaining usage to it.

6) Refund & expiration policy
  - Prepaid collateral expires after expiration_days; default = 365 days for paid SKUs.
  - Refunds allowed within 14 days for self-serve; refunds incur 2% processing fee + prorated usage deduction. Enterprise refundable_percent is negotiable.

7) Accounting & revenue recognition notes (for finance)
  - Use deferred revenue accounting: deposit -> liability; redeem -> recognized revenue based on usage mapping by day. Provide daily export CSV with ledger events.

8) Telemetry & SLOs
  - API availability: 99.95% monthly for bundles APIs.
  - Runtime redemption latency: 95th percentile < 20ms when bundle header present.
  - Reconciliation run success rate: daily job must succeed 7/7 days per week; any missed run triggers oncall paging for finance oncall.
  - Metrics to emit: bundle_deposits, bundle_redemptions, bundle_refunds, bundle_expirations, avg_redeem_latency_ms.

Design details (Design Spec highlights)

- Authorization model: bundles belong to customers; bundle_id can be scoped to an API key or tenant. Only authorized service accounts may redeem reserved_capacity hours.
- Atomic redemption: implement via single-row DB transaction with version column to avoid double-spend (SQL pseudo):
  UPDATE prepaid_bundles SET token_balance = token_balance - :tokens_requested, version = version + 1 WHERE id = :id AND version = :expected_version AND token_balance >= :tokens_requested;
- Fallback rules: define per-bundle policy flags: allow_overage (boolean), prioritize_reserved (boolean). If allow_overage=false and reserved capacity exhausted, return HTTP 429 with error code PREPAID_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED.

UX flows

1) Self-serve purchase
  - Customer clicks Buy > selects SKU > enters payment > purchase completes > bundle deposit credited and visible in Billing UI.
  - UI shows countdown for expiration and breakdown (tokens vs reserved hours).

2) Sales-assisted onboarding
  - Sales creates ephemeral trial CB via Sales Console with trial flags and fixed conversion options. CSM monitors trial usage and triggers conversion playbook if adoption signals pass.

3) Trial-to-paid conversion (playbook)
  - If customer requests conversion, use POST /v1/bundles/{trial_id}/convert which will attempt to create an equivalent paid CB and mark trial CB as converted. Notify finance and CSM.

Rollout plan and milestones

Phase 0 (Q3 2026) - Design & API MVP
  - Finalize SKU definitions and edge-case policies.
  - Implement bundles.create and bundles.get, minimal UI for Billing > Prepaid Credits.
  - Enable trial CB creation via Sales Console only.
  - Telemetry instrumentation for redemption latency and deposit counts.

Phase 1 (Q4 2026) - Runtime integration & self-serve
  - Runtime redemption integration and X-Prepaid-Bundle header support.
  - Self-serve purchase flow and auto-topup UI.
  - Reconciliation export to finance in CSV format.

Phase 2 (Q1 2027) - Enterprise features
  - Refund negotiation flow, invoiced purchase support, and reserved capacity SLA add-ons.
  - Advanced reporting dashboards for CSM/Finance.

Operational runbook (high level)

- Pager triggers: reconciliation failure, daily job misses, unusually high redemption error rate (>0.5% of redeems failing due to DB conflicts), or API error rate spike >3% sustained 5 min.
- Troubleshooting steps:
  1) Check ledger job logs in /jobs/recon and restart job with dry-run flag.
  2) Validate DB replica lag; if lag > 30s, route to infra and pause redemptions for safety.
  3) If double-spend suspected, run diff of ledger vs runtime redemption events and reconcile manually.

Security and compliance notes

- All billing and sensitive payment metadata is stored in PCI-compliant payment gateway; Redwood stores only bundle metadata and ledger events (no raw card data).
- Audit logs: every bundle API call must include caller_id and be logged to long-term audit storage (retention 7 years for enterprise customers on request).

Business & commercial considerations

- Pricing sensitivity experiments: run A/B tests on refundable_percent and expiration_days to measure conversion uplift vs revenue leakage.
- Accounting conservative default: if in doubt, mark expired prepaid as unredeemable after 365 days; sales can negotiate exceptions via ticketing.

Open questions (to resolve before Phase 0 dev kickoff)

- Long-tail SKUs: should we allow custom SKU builder in UI or require Sales to request engineering?
- Cross-tenant redemption: allow child-workspaces to share a single CB? (enterprise asked for this).
- Tax handling & regional pricing: require finance sign-off for multi-currency SKUs.

Ownership and contacts

- Engineering lead: Daniel Ruiz (eng-platform)
- Finance liaison: Sofia Alvarez (finance-legal)
- CSM lead: Priya Nair (customer-success)

Next steps

1) Review this brief with finance and legal by 2026-08-22.
2) Finalize SKU pricing sheet and publish to internal pricing catalog.
3) Kick off API design sprint (2 weeks) and schedule runtime integration spike.

Appendix

Sample CSV export columns for reconciliation:
- date, bundle_id, customer_id, event_type, tokens_delta, reserved_hours_delta, balance_tokens, balance_reserved_hours, ledger_sequence_id

FAQ

Q: Can bundles be transferred between accounts?
A: Not in Phase 1. Transfer requests require sales/finance manual process.

Q: What happens if a bundle purchase charge fails after deposit was created?
A: Create attempts are idempotent; failed payments roll back the DEPOSIT event and create a FAILED_DEPOSIT entry for diagnostics.
